newsitem.title: GERMANY: German SPD seeks early deal on taxes -- Scharping.
newsitem.headline: German SPD seeks early deal on taxes -- Scharping.

text.p: Opposition Social Democrats (SPD) still seek an early resolution with the government on tax reform, despite the collapse of talks on the issue, SPD parliamentary faction leader Rudolf Scharping said.

In an interview with the tabloid Bild newspaper released ahead of its publication on Monday, Scharping said he hoped an agreement could be reached before the tax bill was sent to parliament's mediation committee.
Scharping said the SPD was willing to agree to a reduction in the top income tax rate from the current 53 percent, if the cut could be financed by closing tax loopholes.
He blamed Chancellor Helmut Kohl for the collapse of the negotiations ten days ago, but said he welcomed Kohl's invitation to return to the bargaining table.
"Hopefully he is serious this time," Scharping said. "I still hope to see a result, if possible before the mediation committee between the upper and lower house."
The government is confident of passing the tax bill, which plans net tax cuts of up to 30 billion marks, through the lower house. The cuts are aimed at stimulating investment and jobs creation.
But the bill's near-certain rejection by the SPD majority in the upper house would send it to the mediation committee, where a compromise bill acceptable to both sides would have to be hammered out.
Scharping said the SPD hoped for a tax reform that would cut 2,000 marks from the tax bill of an average family of four.
"Corporations' tax burdens must be lowered first. Then the top income tax rate can fall, if that is financed by closing tax loopholes," he said.
